jati: Shadav-Sampurna (6 notes ascending — Re varja; 7 descending)
time_of_day: Late evening to night — second half of night (9pm to 12am)
aaroh: S G M P n S' (Re omitted; Pa included but treated as alpatva — weak)
avaroh: S' n P M G R S
notes_used: Re shuddh (descent only — varja in ascent), Ga shuddh, Ma shuddh, Pa shuddh but treated as alpatva (weak) in many renditions, Dha shuddh, Ni komal. The omission of Re in ascent and the weak treatment of Pa are both defining features.
characteristic_pakad: n P M G R S
emotional_resonance: feeling unappreciated by a partner or family
feeling emotionally isolated despite being around people
after a disagreement with someone you love
nostalgia and longing for the past
therapy_note: Rageshwari carries a quality of longing that is beautiful rather than painful — like remembering someone deeply loved. The komal Ni gives it a soft, yearning quality, while the omission of Re in the ascent creates a slight incompleteness, a reaching upward that never quite arrives — which is exactly the feeling of longing. Pa's weak status in many treatments further adds to this sense of restrained, unresolved yearning.

bollywood_references.title: Piya Tose Naina Laage Re
bollywood_references.note: Widely considered Rageshwari-based — one of the most beautiful examples of this raag in Bollywood

bollywood_references.title: Ajeeb Dastan Hai Yeh
bollywood_references.note: Rageshwari-influenced evening feel — contains the characteristic komal Ni and yearning quality

bollywood_references.title: Jiya Jale
bollywood_references.note: Uses melodic movement reminiscent of Rageshwari

notes_for_vocalist: Re is strictly forbidden in the ascent — including it immediately shifts the character toward Khamaj. Pa is present but treated with restraint (alpatva) in many classical renditions — do not make it a strong landing note. The komal Ni is the samvadi and the emotional heart of the raag. The phrase 'G M G S' (landing on Sa after Ma and Ga) is very characteristic. This raag is quieter and more intimate than its neighbors — do not sing it loudly.
common_mistakes: Including Re in the aaroh — it is strictly varja (forbidden) in ascent
Treating Pa as a strong note — it has alpatva (weak) status in many treatments
Confusing with Khamaj — Rageshwari has Re varja in aaroh and a different overall movement
Using shuddh Ni — Ni is komal in Rageshwari
variant_notes: Some musicians and schools treat Pa more fully than others — Pa's exact status varies by gharana. The raag is also called Rageshri or Rageshree; some treat these as slightly different variants. Pa treatment is the main point of variation.
